input: Please use this section to tell us about yourself, your skills, achievements and why you want to train as a solicitor and work at Ashurst. (738 words)
output:
I am drawn to commercial practice because I find it stimulating to engage with the business realities behind a client's legal position. As a debt recovery paralegal acting for several 'Big Six' energy providers, I saw how the recent energy crisis had commercial consequences and how trust between those clients and their customers had frayed. To help rebuild that relationship I designed a complaints log so that particular issues, including Ombudsman complaints, could be escalated to the client. I also made sure debtors received clear explanations of complex points, such as Ofgem guidelines during the Supplier of Last Resort process. Those steps contributed to Q2 recoveries exceeding targets by over 150%, with minimal complaints from debtors. Working at the intersection of commercial and legal considerations shows me the practical effect of the law on businesses, which is why I want to train at Ashurst, where lawyers operate as commercial advisers rather than purely legal technicians.

Ashurst specifically appeals because of its genuinely friendly and collaborative culture. Many firms claim friendliness; at the Evening with Ashurst Event I saw that ethos embedded in how the firm works. Trainee Saba Nasrolahi described being involved, after only two weeks, in high-level social inclusion and mobility meetings. That a trainee can contribute to prominent internal discussions demonstrates that Ashurst welcomes trainees and values their input. I thrive in collaborative, accepting environments. As a team leader at the [redacted university] Students' Union I was trusted to create new initiatives, including organising a [redacted event] charity event that involved over 25 staff members and raised over £1,000 for Sport In Mind. Someone who flourishes in a friendly working culture is a natural fit for Ashurst.

During university I also worked as bar staff for my Students' Union. Approaching the role with energy, I made a strong impact and was promoted to Team Leader within just two months. As Team Leader I developed communication, delegation and leadership skills. In freshers week—the busiest period of the year—I managed a different team each night, mostly new staff. I addressed that challenge by introducing myself formally to every team member and explaining their role for the night, and by distributing experienced staff across the venue so newer colleagues could learn by osmosis. That approach produced strong results, including one memorable night when the team achieved record-breaking revenue of over £20,000 in a single day. My interpersonal skills also led to election as social secretary of the Union staff base, where I organised fundraising and social events. I would bring those relationship-building strengths to Ashurst's open, friendly culture.

I also apply strong analytical skills to finish work efficiently and purposefully. When our debt recovery firm took on a new client and received an influx of 1,000 cases shared among three team members, over 100 of those matters concerned the same debtor. Different colleagues were contacting and researching the same individual, creating confusion and inefficiency. I took ownership of those cases and identified two problems: the absence of a single contact point, and data scattered across 100+ files. First, I placed all the files in my name so I could be the ongoing contact for the debtor. Second, I built a spreadsheet capturing the relevant information from the linked accounts, consolidating the matters into one working document so everyone could input information to resolve the disputes. The files closed within 6 weeks and we secured a record-breaking payment of over £300,000. I would apply the same analytical approach at Ashurst to tackle tasks efficiently and effectively.
